reference_traces.rationale: Reviewer-described novelty is supported by final evidence P:S-a42a98bd7e57cdbd5915 and P:S-1797ff6f4ed2e49041ba, which document the biobank-scale integration and independent validation.

Final evidence P:S-4853fe716beb69e21d51 and P:S-a42a98bd7e57cdbd5915 identifies the tripartite model as established by prior ancient-DNA work while stating the present study's population-scale application.
Final evidence P:S-391051222a019f5f98fa and P:S-eff8230b8e26a8f50541 supports the multi-cohort design, including independent Japanese cohorts and UK Biobank East Asian participants.
Final evidence P:S-0775c7832538aa137779 and P:S-e4e4aabdf122f47ede20 reports mainland, sex, age, and alternative population-stratification analyses for the BMI association.
The author response reframed the inference, but final evidence P:S-87bec235050e54840099 still states that BMI-GWAS effect sizes without Jomon ancestry may be biased by residual confounding.

The response added reference-population material, but final evidence P:S-d492ec2451ef48c51939 states that low-coverage pseudo-haploid ancient data restrict finer-resolution modern–ancient associations.

The response describes a proposed evolutionary account but defers variable ancestral analyses; final evidence P:S-62d6273f4389b0a9e372 likewise says post-Jomon genomes are needed to trace inheritance through later lifestyle transitions.
Audit-only resolved presentation issue: final evidence P:S-9db6d7868419002104b8 specifies source-model alternatives and fitting thresholds.
Audit-only resolved utility issue: final evidence P:S-1797ff6f4ed2e49041ba and P:S-7e4426939734344c0a4e describe independent prediction validation and the score construction.

limiting_points.suggested_action: Frame the contribution as a population-scale application and extension of the prior model.
limiting_points.text: The tripartite ancestry framework itself is explicitly presented as previously proposed; the distinct contribution is its large-scale application, phenotypic analysis, and validation rather than introduction of the underlying model.

supporting_points.text: The study integrates ancient genomes with nationwide Biobank Japan data to evaluate geographic and genetic heterogeneity in Jomon ancestry, then validates ancestry-predictive variants in independent Japanese cohorts and UK Biobank East Asian participants.

questions.suggested_action: Clarify the evidentiary boundary between the observed associations and the proposed evolutionary account.
questions.text: What evidence can distinguish selection-linked Jomon segments from later ancestral transmission and environmental change in explaining the BMI-related signal, given that the paper identifies post-Jomon genomes as necessary for resolving that history?

strengths.text: The evidence base combines 171,287 Biobank Japan participants with ancient genomes and includes independent Japanese and UK Biobank East Asian validation cohorts.
The BMI association is examined across the full and mainland samples, sex and age strata, and alternative adjustments for population stratification.

summary.text: The paper applies a prior tripartite ancestry model to biobank-scale Japanese genomic data, evaluates regional and individual variation, tests associations with 80 traits, and develops Jomon-related ancestry markers with independent validation. The central BMI result is supported by several stratification analyses, but the final paper also reports that unadjusted BMI-GWAS effect sizes may retain residual confounding and that limited-resolution ancient data constrain finer ancestry inference.

weaknesses.suggested_action: Distinguish robustness of the association from elimination of residual confounding in its interpretation.
weaknesses.text: The interpretation of the BMI polygenic-score analysis remains limited: adding Jomon ancestry changes the score association, and the final text acknowledges that effect sizes estimated without that covariate may be biased by residual confounding.

weaknesses.suggested_action: Limit fine-resolution ancestry inferences to the resolution supported by the ancient reference data.
weaknesses.text: Individual-level ancestry estimates remain constrained by the ancient reference data: the paper uses low-coverage pseudo-haploid Jomon genomes and acknowledges that this restricts fine-resolution modern–ancient association inference.

revision_ledger.residual_summary: Residual confounding remains an explicit limitation of the BMI-GWAS/PGS interpretation.
Expanded reference handling did not remove the paper's stated low-coverage ancient-data resolution limit.
The evolutionary interpretation is developed, but reconstruction of post-Jomon inheritance remains outstanding.
Source definitions, model alternatives, and fit criteria were added; this is audit-only.
The marker-set prediction purpose and validation were documented; this is audit-only.
